actions.name: exploit public-facing applications to gain initial access
actions.description: Ghost actors obtaining initial access to networks by exploiting public facing applications associated with multiple CVEs including Fortinet FortiOS appliances, Adobe ColdFusion, Microsoft SharePoint, and Microsoft Exchange.

actions.name: upload web shell to compromised server
actions.description: Ghost actors have been observed uploading a web shell to a compromised server.

actions.name: use Windows Command Prompt to download and execute Cobalt Strike Beacon malware
actions.description: Ghost actors leverage Windows Command Prompt and/or PowerShell to download and execute Cobalt Strike Beacon malware implanted on victim systems.

actions.name: use PowerShell to download and execute Cobalt Strike Beacon malware
actions.description: Ghost actors leverage PowerShell to download and execute Cobalt Strike Beacon malware implanted on victim systems.

actions.name: create new local accounts
actions.description: Ghost actors sporadically create new local accounts on victim networks.

actions.name: create new domain accounts
actions.description: Ghost actors sporadically create new domain accounts on victim networks.

actions.name: change passwords for existing accounts
actions.description: Ghost actors change passwords for existing accounts on victim networks.

actions.name: steal process tokens running under SYSTEM user context to impersonate SYSTEM user
actions.description: Ghost actors use built-in Cobalt Strike functions to steal process tokens running under the SYSTEM user context to impersonate the SYSTEM user, often to run Beacon with elevated privileges.

actions.name: attempt privilege escalation using open-source tools
actions.description: Ghost actors have been observed using multiple open-source tools such as SharpZeroLogon, SharpGPPPass, BadPotato, and GodPotato to attempt privilege escalation through exploitation.

actions.name: collect passwords and password hashes using Cobalt Strike hashdump or Mimikatz
actions.description: Ghost actors use the built-in Cobalt Strike function “hashdump” or Mimikatz to collect passwords and/or password hashes to aid unauthorized logins, privilege escalation, or pivoting.

actions.name: disable antivirus software including Windows Defender
actions.description: Ghost actors use Cobalt Strike access to list running processes and determine antivirus software to disable it, frequently running commands to disable Windows Defender with multiple options.

actions.name: use Cobalt Strike and open-source tools for discovery of domain accounts, network shares, and remote systems
actions.description: Ghost actors use Cobalt Strike commands for domain account discovery, SharpShares for network share discovery, and Ladon 911 and SharpNBTScan for remote systems discovery.

actions.name: use WMIC to run PowerShell commands on additional systems for lateral movement
actions.description: Ghost actors use elevated access and Windows Management Instrumentation Command-Line (WMIC) to run PowerShell commands on additional systems to initiate additional Cobalt Strike Beacon infections.

actions.name: abandon attack when lateral movement attempts fail
actions.description: In cases where lateral movement attempts are unsuccessful, Ghost actors have been observed abandoning an attack on a victim.

actions.name: exfiltrate limited data using Cobalt Strike Team Servers and web shells
actions.description: Ghost actors have been observed limited downloading of data to Cobalt Strike Team Servers and limited use of Mega.nz and installed web shells for data exfiltration, typically less than hundreds of gigabytes.

actions.name: use Cobalt Strike Beacon malware and Team Servers for command and control over HTTP and HTTPS
actions.description: Ghost actors rely heavily on Cobalt Strike Beacon malware and Team Servers for command and control operations using HTTP and HTTPS protocols.

actions.name: use legitimate encrypted email services for communication
actions.description: Ghost actors use legitimate email services with traffic encryption features such as Tutanota, Skiff, ProtonMail, Onionmail, and Mailfence for communication with victims.

actions.name: encrypt victim files using ransomware variants
actions.description: Ghost actors use ransomware variants Cring.exe, Ghost.exe, ElysiumO.exe, and Locker.exe to encrypt victim files for ransom.

actions.name: clear Windows Event Logs and delete shadow copies to inhibit system recovery
actions.description: Ghost ransomware payloads clear Windows Event Logs, disable Volume Shadow Copy Service, and delete shadow copies to inhibit system recovery attempts.

actions.name: delete volume shadow copies
actions.description: Ghost actors delete volume shadow copies to inhibit system recovery.
